text:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — saw two OOMs on gpu-node-14 during the 11:30 load test. KV prefix cache used ~18GB and workspace spikes to ~22GB for a few requests, then allocator failed to free fast enough.
Alex Brenner: Any flamegraphs or pprof traces? rough input sizes? :eyes:
Maya Chen: attaching quick profiler snippet, repro steps in thread below. Most requests are long-context chat (~6k tokens) plus a 2k prefix cache hit. Profiler shows a few big workspace allocs around kernel selection for multihead attention.
Maya Chen: ```
# perf dump (trimmed)
alloc_workspace_kb  : 22000000
kv_cache_total_kb   : 18400000
kernel_select_time_ms: 12.4
attention_kernel_id : fused_fp16_opt
batching_wait_ms    : 8.9
``` 
Dmitry Ivanov: Hmm. Two immediate levers: (1) allocator tuning to prefer pre-reserved workspace pools + reuse buffers across attention kernels, (2) prefix cache shard sizing / TTL to reduce resident KV memory.
Samir Patel: For allocator, I think switching workspace_sizing factor to 0.35 helped us in staging — lowers max per-request workspace and forces earlier fallback to streaming kernels. That avoided OOMs but added ~1.8ms p99 for some workloads.
Maya Chen: Can you paste the exact config change you tested, Sam? We need to quantify latency vs memory tradeoffs.
Samir Patel: ```
# old
workspace_sizing: 0.5
# new
workspace_sizing: 0.35
reusable_buffers: true
buffer_reuse_strategy: cross_kernel
mempool_backend: cuMemPool
``` 
Dmitry Ivanov: Also recommend aggressive buffer reuse for KV operations; reuse the same pinned staging buffer for copy-in/out instead of allocating per-shard. That saved ~2.2GB in a local perf run.
Rachel Ng: On prefix cache side: we should split shards by hit-rate. High-hit prefixes get larger shard TTL and fewer evictions; cold prefixes drop TTL to 60s and compact shards aggressively. We measured hit-rate uplift when we rebalanced shards by traffic fingerprint.
Alex Brenner: Good. But how do we measure the UX impact? Lower TTL may increase recomputation cost (tokens) vs reduced OOMs. We need a dashboard: bytes-resident vs prefix_hit_latency vs recompute_tokens/sec.
Maya Chen: I'll add a quick dashboard panel for kv_resident_bytes, prefix_hit_rate, and re-gen token count. Also running an A/B on workspace_sizing 0.5 vs 0.35 for the same workload.
infra-bot: alert — gpu-node-14 had OOM at 2026-03-15T11:30:12Z (investigation ticket #INV-4123)
Dmitry Ivanov: One extra idea — kernel selection policy: prefer lower-memory kernel variants when predicted workspace + KV_sum > 0.8 * gpu_free. We can compute prediction at routing time and swap kernel variant before dispatch.
Samir Patel: That's the neat part; if we can cheaply predict memory footprint per request (seq_len distribution + prefix_shard_size) we can route to a compact kernel or a different model quantization variant.
Rachel Ng: For the prefix cache provisioning doc, I'll propose: default shard_size=64MB, dynamic scale to 128MB for shards with >50% hit_rate, TTL 300s -> 60s fallback for tail. Include an emergency eviction trigger when free_mem < 1.2x workspace_budget.
Maya Chen: Action items: 1) Sam — run A/B for workspace_sizing 0.35 vs 0.5 and post numbers (p50/p95/p99 latency, OOM count, resident_kv_bytes). 2) Dmitry — prototype routing-time memory predictor + kernel fallback (P0: simulation). 3) Rachel — write shard sizing TTL proposal and perf impact estimates. I'll coordinate dashboard and follow-up.
Alex Brenner: Sounds good. If A/B looks okay, we can roll config change behind a canary and enable buffer reuse feature flag. :thumbsup:
Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — I'll update INV-4123 with these notes.
